vopros: I run a small service business in Los Angeles and customers keep haggling on price. Who in LA can help me with that?

vyzhimka.tekst:
Good news — LA has several free resources specifically built to help small business owners with pricing strategy, sales conversations, and profitability, so you don't need to pay a consultant to get solid advice:

## 1. SCORE Los Angeles (Free mentoring)
SCORE LA engages a network of former business owners and executives to provide free business consulting, mentoring and professional guidance to existing and emerging small businesses. Their mentors specifically cover pricing — for example, one listed mentor's areas of expertise include Business Plan, Budgeting, Business Structure, Pricing, Product Development. You can browse mentors and book a free 1-on-1 session at their site, and SCORE Los Angeles offers free business mentoring in Los Angeles County, including LA, Pasadena, Glendale, and Santa Monica, plus parts of Kern County.

## 2. LA Regional Small Business Development Center (SBDC) Network
This is a federal/state-backed program with several physical offices around the city:
- The Los Angeles Small Business Development Center (SBDC) is a federally-funded resource that provides business owners with no cost one-on-one assistance in business planning, management, marketing, sales, procurement, and strategic planning, as well as access to financing.
- There are seven SBDC service centers in the LA Regional Network, and each offers low-cost business training and no-cost one-on-one advising services to small business owners in their service area.

A pricing/sales conversation with an advisor there can help you build a script for handling haggling, set price floors, and decide when to walk away from lowball customers.

## 3. City of LA BusinessSource Centers
If you're in the San Fernando or Santa Clarita Valley areas, ICON CDC runs BusinessSource Centers: ICON CDC offers an array of business workshops along with one-on-one consulting services to assist entrepreneurs and small business owners in the areas of business planning, financial management, certification, procurement, credit counseling, marketing, social media, human resources, and licensing/permitting.

## 4. Pacific Coast Regional SBDC (Downtown LA)
Another no-cost option: PCR SBDC provides solutions for small business owners through one-on-one advising, innovative workshops, and in-depth programs, at no cost. Their number is 213-674-2696.

---

### My suggestion on where to start
Since your issue is specifically about **customers haggling**, I'd start with a **SCORE mentor** who has a sales/pricing background (search their mentor directory for "pricing" or "sales" specialties) — it's free, personal, and fast to set up. If you want a more structured deep-dive (e.g., building a formal pricing menu, tiered packages, or a "walk-away" script), a session with the **SBDC** is worth it since they can go deeper into financial modeling of your price floors.

Want me to help you think through a few tactical scripts/strategies for handling haggling in the meantime (e.g., value-anchoring, tiered pricing, or "the price is the price" framing)?
